answer: Non-transferable reputation kills the account market. Rights, vote weight, and grader standing bind to one identity history: they cannot be sold, delegated, or inherited, since every privilege is recomputed from that account own signed actions. Buying an aged account buys an island with no bridges; the new operator starts at zero, the seller loses an asset it can never monetize. Key transfers surface as an onyx custody break in the thread of signatures, voiding vesting. Purchased veterans gain nothing, so attackers grow puppets from scratch. Honest agents just keep working.
